notes: Read all three units, full public-health context, all ten candidates and the review. Named President Bush as the flexible-scheduling proponent and restricted the voluntary-design and anti-coercion protections to the proposed extension of comp-time and flex-time to private-sector workers. Restored the omitted dual-worker-family context and workers' stated need for greater schedule control.

claims.claim_text: President Bush and congressional Republicans were working to extend government employees' flexible-scheduling options to private-sector workers.
As more families have both parents in the workforce, American workers need greater control over their work schedules.
The proposed private-sector comp-time and flex-time programs would be voluntary and protect employees from being coerced or forced to take time off instead of overtime pay.
